title: Collapse overlapping exons and derive non-exonic genome intervals
repo_revision: master branch, inspected 2026-09-29; exact HEAD SHA unavailable through inspected GitHub views (latest release v2.31.1 points to 705ccfd, not asserted as master HEAD)

sources.locator: 'bedtools merge' and 'bedtools complement' sections, approx lines 429-554
merge combines overlapping or book-ended intervals; options for grouped columns
complement usage with genome sizes file

scientific_use: Merge overlapping/book-ended exon intervals into contiguous genomic spans, optionally count constituent annotations or merge nearby intervals within a chosen distance; use a genome-size file to derive the complement, i.e. non-exonic intervals. This can create a nonredundant exon mask and candidate intronic/intergenic space.
tool_role_basis: Tutorial uses bedtools merge/complement and UNIX sort over BED and a chromosome-size file; the tools implement the interval operations.

inputs.processing_stage: reference annotation; must sort by chromosome and start for merge
reference assembly metadata required for complement

outputs.meaning: Merged nonredundant intervals with optional counts or aggregated fields
Intervals not covered by exon annotations within specified genome bounds

dependencies: Genome file matching exact reference assembly and chromosome naming
Choice of merge distance and field aggregation changes biological interpretation

tutorial lines 493-503 shows merging within 1000 bp

limitations: No precise genome assembly for tutorial files is established in the inspected passage; complement is invalid if genome file and annotation differ.
